text:
maria: Heads-up — after the NCCL bump this morning (3.5.2) we're seeing a progressive throughput drop for model-ranker on eu-west3. 99th p50 tails climbing, and some jobs show stuck p2p queues. Anyone else? :eyes:

alex: I saw a small uptick in NVLink error counters around 08:12 UTC on node pool-gpu-ef. Could be p2p retransmits causing backpressure. Can you paste the pod/node ids?

maria: pod=ranker-7f8c, node=gpu-ew3-12. Logs attached below (snippets).

maria: ```
# nvidia-smi topo --matrix
        GPU0 GPU1 CPU
GPU0     X   NV1   0
GPU1   NV1     X   0

# dmesg | tail -n 8
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:81:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568012] NVRM: GPU 0000:82:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

jon: Oof. "fallen off the bus" often points to driver/kernel interactions. Which kernel and driver did we roll to with the NCCL upgrade?

maria: kernel=6.4.14, nvidia-driver=535.86, nccl=3.5.2. Canary matrix had passed for our small set but rollout was wider than the canary.

olivia: Can we run nccl tests on the affected node to reproduce? `nccl-tests -b 8 -e 512M -f 2` should show allgather/allreduce hangs if it's p2p. I can queue a job.

luis: Adding telemetry: /metrics shows p2p_queue_len spike on node gpu-ew3-12 at 08:10-08:25, memory usage on NVMe stayed normal but GPU mem climbed and didn't drop between requests — possible KV cache leak + stalled collectives.

maria: Interesting. Throughput loss correlates with p2p queue growth and retry counters in driver logs. No OOMs reported in kube.

sre-bot: deploy-bot reports: rollout id r-2023-nccl-3-5 completed in eu-west3 at 07:50 UTC. Canary success: 5/5. Production rollout: 90% nodes updated by 08:05.

alex: Canary size was small and didn't hit mixed-arch backends (some nodes have mixed Ampere+Hopper). Mixed arch + nccl 3.5 has known edge-case for p2p fallback leading to serialization.

jon: Quick mitigation options: 1) pin pods to nodes still on previous nccl via nodeSelector (slow), 2) rollback nccl package on fleet (fast but needs coordination), 3) apply nccl env override to force p2p disable for affected topologies (trial). Which is feasible?

olivia: I can test env override on one staging node: `export NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` and run load. If that restores throughput, it's a viable stopgap. Will run now.

maria: If we roll back, we need to estimate cost: rolling back across eu-west3 will rollback ~120 GPU nodes; expected ~2 hours of coord + ephemeral perf hits. If we keep degraded, customer-facing SLOs will be impacted and cost per inference goes up ~30% due to retries.

luis: For data collection — capture `nvprof`/nsight logs for a stuck job, `strace` of the inference process to confirm blocked syscalls, and `nccl-debug` traces (set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO). Save to s3://redwood-debug/eu-west3/2234569999/

olivia: Test update: with NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 on staging node, p2p_queue_len stayed low and throughput recovered to ~98% baseline. Will run a 30m soak.

alex: Good. If soak holds, we can push env override as a cluster-wide config for eu-west3 via our runtime config service while we coordinate a full rollback or wait for vendor patch. It's less risky than immediate fleet rollback.

maria: Agreed. Action items: 1) olivia to run 30m soak and confirm metrics (ETA 40m). 2) luis to collect driver and nccl traces from gpu-ew3-12 and upload. 3) jon/alex to draft rollback runbook if soak fails. 4) ops to alert customers if SLOs will be impacted > 15m.

deploy-bot: runbook-create: /runbooks/nccl-3-5-incident created by jon at 2234570300.

maria: Thanks all. I'll update incident page with the soak result and next steps. :thumbsup:
